# Level 1 Student Handout: Deepening Belief & the Quran
**Age Group:** Ages 6-8 (Level 1 Track: Primary Stage 1)  
**Core Strands:** The Holy Quran, Respect for the Mushaf, Surah Al-Fatihah, Surah Al-Ikhlas, and Everyday Quranic Du'as  
**Classical Text Spine:** *'Aqidat al-'Awamm* (The Heavenly Books) and *Mukhtasar al-Akhdari*  
**Riwayah & Surah Target:** Hafs 'an 'Asim and Warsh 'an Nafi' (Juz' 30: Surah Al-Fatihah, Surah Al-Ikhlas, Surah Al-Falaq, and Surah An-Nas)

---

## 1. The Most Beautiful Book in the World

The **Holy Quran** is Allah's direct message of love, guidance, and light sent to all humanity:

* **The Speech of Allah:** The Quran is not authored by human beings; it is the pure, eternal Words of Allah.
* **The Archangel of Light:** Allah sent the great Archangel **Jibril** (AS) from the heavens to convey these exact Arabic words into the heart of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.
* **The Great Reward for Recitation:** The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ said:  
  > *"Whoever recites a letter from the Book of Allah will be credited with a good deed, and a good deed receives a tenfold reward. I do not say that Alif-Lam-Mim is one letter, but Alif is a letter, Lam is a letter, and Mim is a letter."* (Jami' at-Tirmidhi 2910, Hasan Sahih)  
  This means reciting just "Alif-Lam-Mim" earns thirty rewards (*Hasanat*)!
* **A Guide for Living:** The Quran teaches us how to worship Allah, how to speak the truth, how to honor parents and teachers, and how to reach Paradise (*Jannah*).

---

## 2. How We Care for and Respect the Mushaf

A printed physical copy of the Holy Quran is called a **Mushaf**. Because it holds the sacred Words of Allah, Muslims show it profound love and respect:

1. **Purity with Wudu:** We make sure our hands and body are clean with fresh **Wudu** before holding the Mushaf.
2. **Hold with Both Hands:** We hold the Mushaf gently with both hands, showing reverence for the book of Allah.
3. **High and Clean Places:** We never place the Mushaf on the floor, under other books, or where people walk. We place it on a clean high shelf or a wooden bookstand (*Rihl*).
4. **Attentive Listening:** When the Quran is recited, we sit quietly, listen carefully, and refrain from noisy play or distracting chatter.

---

## 3. Surah Al-Fatihah and Surah Al-Ikhlas

### A. Surah Al-Fatihah (The Opening: Surah 1)
Every single rak'ah of our daily prayer begins with **Surah Al-Fatihah** (The Opening), known as the Mother of the Quran (*Umm al-Kitab*):
* **بِسْمِ ٱللَّٰهِ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ** (*"In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful."*)
* **ٱلْحَمْدُ لِلَّٰهِ رَبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ** (*"All praise belongs to Allah, Lord of all the worlds."*)
* **ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ** (*"The Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful."*)
* **مَٰلِكِ يَوْمِ ٱلدِّينِ** (*"Master of the Day of Judgment."*)
* **إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ وَإِيَّاكَ نَسْتَعِينُ** (*"You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help."*)
* **ٱهْدِنَا ٱلصِّرَٰطَ ٱلْمُسْتَقِيمَ** (*"Guide us on the Straight Path!"*)
* **صِرَٰطَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ غَيْرِ ٱلْمَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا ٱلضَّآلِّينَ** (*"The path of those You have blessed, not of those who earned anger, nor those who are lost."*)

When we finish reciting Surah Al-Fatihah, we say softly: **"Ameen"** (O Allah, accept our prayer!).

### B. Surah Al-Ikhlas (Pure Faith: Surah 112)
Surah Al-Ikhlas is a short, powerful surah that teaches us the pure Oneness of Allah (*Tawhid*). The Prophet ﷺ explained that reciting it is equivalent in reward to reciting one-third of the Quran (Sahih al-Bukhari 5013):
* **قُلْ هُوَ ٱللَّهُ أَحَدٌ** (*"Say: He is Allah, the One."*)
* **ٱللَّهُ ٱلصَّمَدُ** (*"Allah, the Eternal Refuge [Al-Samad]: all creation relies upon Him, and He needs no one."*)
* **لَمْ يَلِدْ وَلَمْ يُولَدْ** (*"He neither begets nor was He begotten: He has no children and no parents."*)
* **وَلَمْ يَكُن لَّهُۥ كُفُوًا أَحَدٌۢ** (*"And there is none comparable unto Him."*)

---

## 4. The Two Protecting Surahs: Al-Falaq and An-Nas

Before going to sleep, the Prophet ﷺ taught us to cup our hands together, recite Surah Al-Ikhlas, Surah Al-Falaq, and Surah An-Nas, gently blow into our palms, and wipe over our head, face, and front of the body:
1. **Surah Al-Falaq (The Daybreak):** We ask Allah to protect us from the darkness of the night, jealousy, and harm.
2. **Surah An-Nas (Mankind):** We ask Allah, the Lord and King of humanity, to protect our hearts from negative thoughts and whispered doubts.

---

## 5. Curriculum Anchors in Practice

1. **Daily Recitation Habit:** Practice reciting a short surah like Surah Al-Ikhlas every morning and evening. Remember that each Arabic letter earns ten good deeds!
2. **Handling the Quran with Care:** Inspect where the Mushaf is kept in your home. Ensure it rests on a clean, elevated table or bookshelf away from clutter.
3. **Bedtime Sunnah:** Tonight before sleep, sit up, cup your hands, recite the three Qul surahs (Al-Ikhlas, Al-Falaq, and An-Nas), and thank Allah for all your blessings.

(A) A desert philosopher in ancient Arabia
(B) A royal scribe in a palace
(C) A council of poets in Makkah

(A) Surah Al-Fatihah

(D) Surah Al-Mulk

(A) Run around and shout in the room
(B) Increase the television volume
(C) Listen quietly, attentively, and respectfully

(A) Surah Al-Fil
(B) Surah Quraysh

(D) Surah Al-Ikhlas

Vocabulary Bank: Words, Fatihah, Ten

6. Words
7. Fatihah
8. Ten

* Surah Al-Ikhlas ─── Teaches pure Tawhid that Allah is One and Al-Samad

* Surah Al-Fatihah ─── The opening chapter of the Quran recited in every rak'ah
* Surah Al-Ikhlas ─── Teaches pure Tawhid that Allah is One and Al-Samad

# Level 2 Student Handout: Deepening Belief & the Quran
**Age Group:** Ages 8-10 (Level 2 Track: Primary Stage 2)  
**Core Strands:** 'Ulum al-Quran, Tajweed Foundations, Tafkhim & Tarqiq, Madd, and Tafsir of Short Surahs  
**Classical Text Spine:** *'Aqidat al-'Awamm* and Foundational Principles of Tajweed  
**Riwayah & Surah Target:** Hafs 'an 'Asim and Warsh 'an Nafi' (Juz' 30: Surah Al-Ikhlas, Surah Ash-Sharh, and Surah Ad-Duha)

---

## 1. How the Holy Quran Was Revealed and Preserved

The revelation of the Holy Quran is the supreme historical event guiding the Muslim community. It took place in two stages:

1. **The Single Heavenly Descent (*Inzal*):** On the Night of Power (**Laylat al-Qadr**) in the month of Ramadan, Allah sent the entire Quran from the Preserved Tablet (*Al-Lawh al-Mahfuz*) to the House of Glory (*Bayt al-'Izzah*) in the lowest heaven (Surah Al-Qadr 97:1).
2. **The Gradual Descent to Humanity (*Tanzil*):** Over a period of **twenty-three years**, Archangel Jibril brought verses down to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ in stages (thirteen years in Makkah and ten years in Madinah) addressing real-life situations, questions, and community needs (Surah Al-Isra' 17:106).

### The Two Divisions of Surahs

| Division | Historical Period | Primary Themes and Style |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Makki Surahs** | Revealed before the Great Migration (*Hijrah*) to Madinah | Powerful, rhythmic verses focusing on pure monotheism (*Tawhid*), the Day of Resurrection, moral purification, and steadfastness under trial. |
| **Madani Surahs** | Revealed after the Hijrah to Madinah | Detailed legislative guidance concerning prayer, fasting, charity (*Zakah*), community justice, family laws, and mutual covenants. |

---

## 2. Tajweed Basics: Beautifying Our Recitation

Allah states in Surah Al-Muzzammil (73:4):  
> **وَرَتِّلِ ٱلْقُرْءَانَ تَرْتِيلًا**  
> *"And recite the Quran with measured, clear recitation."*

**Tajweed** means reciting each Arabic letter from its correct point of origin (*Makhraj*) with its proper attributes (*Sifat*). At Level 2, we master two fundamental concepts:

### A. Tafkhim (Heavy) vs Tarqiq (Light)
* **Tafkhim (Heavy / Full-Mouth Pronunciation):** When reciting a heavy letter, the back of the tongue rises toward the roof of the mouth, filling the mouth with a deep, full resonance. There are seven permanently heavy letters known as **Huruf al-Isti'la'**, gathered in the phrase:  
  **خُصَّ ضَغْطٍ قِظْ** (*Kha, Sad, Dad, Ghayn, Ta, Qaf, Zha*).  
  *Example:* Recite **صَ** (*Sad*) with a deep, full mouth, distinctly different from **سَ** (*Seen*), which is pronounced lightly.
* **Tarqiq (Light / Flat Pronunciation):** All letters other than the seven heavy letters are pronounced with a flat, relaxed tongue position (*Tarqiq*), smiling gently without puffing the cheeks (except the letters Lam and Ra, which have special conditions).

### B. Natural Elongation (Madd Tabee'ee)
When an Alif appears after a Fathah, a Waw after a Dammah, or a Ya after a Kasrah, we gently stretch the vowel for exactly **two counts (beats)**:  
> **قَالَ** (*Qaa-la*), **يَقُولُ** (*Ya-qoo-lu*), **قِيلَ** (*Qee-la*).

---

## 3. Tafsir and Reflection: Hope and Pure Faith

### A. Surah Al-Ikhlas (112:1-4): Pure Faith and Al-Samad
Surah Al-Ikhlas teaches pure monotheism. In this surah, Allah reveals His Name **Al-Samad**:  
> **ٱللَّهُ ٱلصَّمَدُ** (*"Allah, the Eternal Refuge [Al-Samad]"*)  
*Al-Samad* means the Self-Sufficient Master upon Whom every created being wholly depends for food, air, guidance, and life, while He has no need of anything or anyone.

### B. Surah Ad-Duha (The Morning Sun: Surah 93)
When revelation paused temporarily in Makkah, opponents mocked the Prophet ﷺ. Allah revealed Surah Ad-Duha to reassure him:  
> **مَا وَدَّعَكَ رَبُّكَ وَمَا قَلَىٰ • وَلَلْـَٔاخِرَةُ خَيْرٌۭ لَّكَ مِنَ ٱلْأُولَىٰ**  
> *"Your Lord has neither forsaken you, nor is He displeased. And surely the Hereafter will be better for you than this first life."* (93:3-4)  
Allah reminded the Prophet ﷺ of past mercies: He was an orphan and Allah sheltered him; he sought guidance and Allah guided him. Therefore, Muslims must treat orphans with gentleness and never turn away a seeker of help.

### C. Surah Ash-Sharh (The Expansion: Surah 94)
Allah grants believers a permanent promise of divine relief:  
> **فَإِنَّ مَعَ ٱلْعُسْرِ يُسْرًا • إِنَّ مَعَ ٱلْعُسْرِ يُسْرًا**  
> *"For indeed, with hardship comes ease! Truly, with hardship comes ease!"* (94:5-6)  
Notice that relief accompanies hardship; whenever a difficulty arises in school or life, patience (*Sabr*) unlocks Allah's arriving assistance.

---

## 4. Curriculum Anchors in Practice

1. **Practicing Tafkhim and Tarqiq:** Recite Surah Al-Fatihah slowly. Pay attention to the letter *Sad* in *Sirat* (heavy with Tafkhim) versus the letter *Seen* in *Bismillah* (light with Tarqiq).
2. **Reflecting on Al-Samad:** Whenever you need help with schoolwork or feel worried, remember that Allah is *Al-Samad*. Raise your hands in Du'a and ask Him directly.
3. **Patience Brings Ease:** Think of a time when a difficult chore or study task became easier with persistence. How does Surah Ash-Sharh (94:5-6) comfort you when you face a challenge?

**Age Group:** Ages 8-10 (Level 2 Track)  
**Focus:** 23 Years of Revelation, Tajweed, Tafkhim, and Surah Al-Ikhlas  

---

## Part A: Multiple Choice

### 1. Over how many years was the Noble Quran revealed gradually to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ?
(A) 23 years (13 in Makkah and 10 in Madinah)
(B) 1 year during Ramadan
(C) 10 years in Madinah only
(D) 40 years from youth

### 2. What was the primary focus of the Makkan surahs revealed during the first thirteen years before the Hijrah?
(A) Complex inheritance calculations and municipal courts
(B) Guidelines for regional trade agreements
(C) Pure Tawhid, the Day of Judgment, moral steadfastness, and building sincere faith
(D) Rules for international postal communications

### 3. What does the divine Name *Al-Samad* signify in Surah Al-Ikhlas?
(A) The Owner of fertile desert pastures
(B) The Guardian of physical strength
(C) The Designer of celestial stars
(D) The Eternal, Self-Sufficient Refuge upon Whom all creation relies, while He needs nothing

### 4. In the science of Tajweed, what is the term for pronouncing a heavy letter with a full, resonant mouth sound?
(A) Tarqiq (Light pronunciation)
(B) Tafkhim (Heavy, full-mouth pronunciation)
(C) Ghunnah (Nasalization)
(D) Waqf (Pausing)

### 5. Why did Allah reveal the Quran gradually in stages (*Tanzil*) over twenty-three years rather than all at once?
(A) To strengthen the heart of the Prophet ﷺ and allow believers to memorize, understand, and apply its guidance step-by-step
(B) Because writing parchment was unavailable in early Makkah
(C) Because early companions requested fewer verses per season
(D) To match the seasonal caravan travel schedules between Syria and Yemen

---

## Part B: Fill in the Blanks
Vocabulary Bank: Twenty-three, Makki, Tafkhim, Al-Samad

6. The Quran was revealed gradually over a total period of ______ years.
7. Surahs revealed before the historic Hijrah to Madinah are called ______ surahs.
8. Pronouncing a letter with a full, deep mouth resonance in Tajweed is called ______.
9. The divine Name meaning the Self-Sufficient Refuge in Surah Al-Ikhlas is ______.

### Fill in the Blanks Key
6. Twenty-three
7. Makki
8. Tafkhim
9. Al-Samad

---

## Part C: Matching Pairs
* Tafkhim ─── Heavy, full-mouth pronunciation of the seven Isti'la' letters
* Madd Tabee'ee ─── Natural two-count elongation of long vowel sounds
* Twenty-three Years ─── The total timeline of gradual Quranic revelation
* Al-Samad ─── The Eternal Refuge upon Whom all creation relies

### Matching Key
* Tafkhim ─── Heavy, full-mouth pronunciation of the seven Isti'la' letters
* Madd Tabee'ee ─── Natural two-count elongation of long vowel sounds
* Twenty-three Years ─── The total timeline of gradual Quranic revelation
* Al-Samad ─── The Eternal Refuge upon Whom all creation relies

---

## Part D: Reflection

10. Why is it easier to build lasting good habits when we learn them step-by-step, just as the Quran was revealed gradually over twenty-three years?

### Reflection Rubric
* **Full Understanding:** Student explains that gradual learning prevents feeling overwhelmed, allows time for practice, and leads to deep understanding and lasting character habits.
* **Basic Understanding:** Student notes that learning slowly is easier without connecting it to habit formation or the wisdom of gradual Quranic revelation.

---

## Teacher Answer Key
1. A - The Quran was revealed over 23 years (13 in Makkah and 10 in Madinah).
2. C - Makkan surahs focused on establishing Tawhid, the Hereafter, and steadfast faith.
3. D - Al-Samad means the Self-Sufficient Master upon Whom all creation depends.
4. B - Tafkhim refers to the heavy, resonant pronunciation produced by the seven letters of Isti'la'.
5. A - Surah Al-Furqan (25:32) explains that gradual revelation strengthened the Prophet's heart and facilitated comprehension.

# Level 3 Student Handout: Deepening Belief & the Quran
**Age Group:** Ages 10-12 (Level 3 Track: Years 5 & 6)  
**Topics:** The Miraculous Quran, Tajweed Rules (Noon Sakinah & Qalqalah), Thematic Tafsir of Surah An-Naba', Sincerity (Ikhlas), and Introduction to Hadith & Madhhabs  
**Classical Text Spine:** *Tafsir Ibn Kathir*, *Matn al-Jazariyyah*, *Al-Murshid al-Mu'in*, and *Al-Arba'in al-Nawawiyyah*  
**Riwayah & Tajweed:** Hafs 'an 'Asim and Warsh 'an Nafi' (Juz' 30: Surah An-Naba' and Surah Al-'Asr; Noon Sakinah & Qalqalah)

---

## 1. The Living Miracle: The Noble Speech of Allah

The Holy Quran is the literal, uncreated speech of Allah revealed through Archangel Jibril (AS) to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ over a period of twenty-three years (thirteen in Makkah and ten in Madinah). Unlike previous scriptures that were entrusted to human scribes and suffered alterations over centuries, Allah guaranteed the direct preservation of the Quran:  
> **إِنَّا نَحْنُ نَزَّلْنَا ٱلذِّكْرَ وَإِنَّا لَهُۥ لَحَٰفِظُونَ**  
> *"Indeed, it is We who sent down the Quran and indeed, We will be its guardian."* (Surah Al-Hijr 15:9)

---

## 2. The Science of Tajweed: Noon Sakinah & Qalqalah

When reciting the Quran, we beautify our recitation by applying the classical rules of **Tajweed** (precise articulation and rhythmic delivery):

### The Four Rules of Noon Sakinah (نْ) and Tanween (ً ٍ ٌ)

| Number & Rule | Arabic Name | Meaning & Articulation | Trigger Letters | Practical Example |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **1. Al-Izhar al-Halqi** | الإِظْهَارُ الْحَلْقِيُّ | Clear, distinct pronunciation of the Noon without nasal hum (*Ghunnah*). | The 6 throat letters: **Hamzah (ء), Ha (هـ), 'Ayn (ع), Ha (ح), Ghayn (غ), Kha (خ)** | *Man amana*, *Min khawf* |
| **2. Al-Idgham** | الإِدْغَامُ | Merging the Noon into the following letter. Has two sub-types: | | |
| **2a. With Ghunnah** | إدغام بغنة | Merging with a 2-count nasal resonance (*Ghunnah*). | The 4 letters of **Yanmu (ي ن م و)** | *Man yaqul*, *Min ma'* |
| **2b. Without Ghunnah** | إدغام بغير غنة | Complete merging without nasal hum (*Idgham Kamil*). | The 2 letters **Lam (ل) and Ra (ر)** | *Mil-ladunhu*, *Mir-rabbihim* |
| **3. Al-Iqlab** | الإِقْلابُ | Converting the Noon sound into a soft, hidden **Meem (م)** with a 2-count Ghunnah. | The single letter **Ba (ب)** | *Min ba'di* (recited *Mim-ba'di*) |
| **4. Al-Ikhfa' al-Haqiqi** | الإِخْفَاءُ الْحَقِيقِيُّ | Concealing the Noon between Izhar and Idgham with a gentle 2-count nasal tone. | The remaining **15 letters** of the Arabic alphabet | *Min duni*, *Anfusakum* |

### The Rule of Qalqalah (Echoing Vibration)
When any of the five letters of **Qutbu Jaddin (ق ط ب ج د)** carries a Sukun (or you stop upon it), the vocal point rebounds with a crisp echo:
* **Minor Qalqalah (Sughra):** When the letter occurs in the middle of a word (e.g. *Yaq-ta'un*, *Ab-na'ahum*).
* **Major Qalqalah (Kubra):** When stopping upon the letter at the end of an ayah (e.g. *Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad [d]*).

---

## 3. Thematic Tafsir: Surah An-Naba' (The Great News: Surah 78)

Surah An-Naba' opens the 30th Juz' of the Quran, addressing the skepticism of the Makkan disbelievers regarding the Day of Resurrection:

### The Three Thematic Sections of Surah An-Naba'
1. **Cosmic Signs of Divine Omnipotence (Verses 6-16):**  
   Allah directs human contemplation to His observable creation to demonstrate His power to resurrect humanity:
   * The earth spread out as a stable resting place (*Mihada*).
   * The mountains driven into the crust as stabilizing pegs (*Awtada*).
   * The creation of humanity in pairs, the gift of night for rest, the daytime for seeking livelihood, the seven heavens, the radiant sun (*Siraja Wahhaja*), and rain clouds producing abundant gardens.
2. **The Day of Sorting (*Yawm al-Fasl*: Verses 17-30):**  
   The blowing of the Trumpet, the opening of heavenly gates, the dispersal of mountains, and the severe consequence awaiting persistent arrogance in Jahannam.
3. **The Reward of the Righteous (*Al-Muttaqun*: Verses 31-40):**  
   Enclosed gardens, cooling beverages, and peaceful tranquility for those who guarded their faith. The surah concludes with a solemn reminder: on that Day, the unrepentant will gaze upon their deeds and lament:  
   > **يَٰلَيْتَنِى كُنتُ تُرَٰبًۢا**  
   > *"Oh, I wish that I were dust!"* (78:40)

---

## 4. Intention, Hadith Sciences, and Following a Madhhab

To deepen our understanding of faith and sacred practice, Level 3 students learn four foundational sciences:

### A. Intention (Niyyah) & Sincerity (Ikhlas)
The first hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari states:  
> *"Actions are judged only by intentions, and every person will have only what they intended."* (Sahih al-Bukhari 1, Sahih Muslim 1907)  
* **Ikhlas (Sincerity):** Doing an act purely for Allah's pleasure alone.
* **Riya' (Ostentation):** Performing worship to impress other people. The Prophet ﷺ warned that Riya' is "minor shirk" because it seeks praise from creation rather than the Creator.
* **Ash'ari Kasb (Acquisition):** Ash'ari theology teaches that Allah creates the act, while the human being chooses and acquires (*Kasb*) responsibility through their intention and free will.

### B. Tafsir of Surah Al-'Asr (Time: Surah 103)
Imam al-Shafi'i observed: *"If Allah had revealed only this surah, it would have sufficed humanity."* In three short verses, Allah swears by Time and establishes the four conditions of true success:
1. True Faith (*Iman*).
2. Righteous deeds (*'Amal Salih*).
3. Advising one another to truth and justice (*Al-Tawasi bil-Haqq*).
4. Advising one another to patient perseverance (*Al-Tawasi bil-Sabr*).

### C. Introduction to Hadith Sciences
A Prophetic Hadith consists of two elements:
* **The Isnad (Chain):** The sequence of verified narrators transmitting the report from one generation to the next.
* **The Matn (Text):** The actual spoken words or described action of the Prophet ﷺ.  
Scholars classify Hadith into three major categories based on narrator integrity and continuous chains: **Sahih** (Sound/Authentic), **Hasan** (Good/Reliable), and **Da'if** (Weak). The most authoritative early hadith texts include *Al-Muwatta'* of Imam Malik and the Sahih compilations of al-Bukhari and Muslim.

### D. Why Muslims Follow a Sunni Madhhab
No single individual can independently interpret thousands of Quranic verses and hadiths without systematic training. The four Sunni schools of jurisprudence (**Hanafi, Maliki, Shafi'i, and Hanbali**) represent four verified legal methodologies developed by master scholars. In the Maliki school, Imam Malik prioritized the continuous inherited practice of the people of Madinah (*'Amal Ahl al-Madinah*), providing an unbroken living transmission of the Prophetic Sunnah.

---

## 5. Curriculum Anchors in Practice

1. **Purifying Your Daily Intention:** Before beginning study, chores, or sports, make a silent intention (*Niyyah*): *"O Allah, I am doing this to gain strength, knowledge, and discipline to serve You and help my family."*
2. **Applying the Four Rules of Noon Sakinah:** Read the opening page of Juz' 'Amma (Surah An-Naba'). Identify at least one instance of Izhar, Idgham, Iqlab, and Ikhfa', reciting each with correct Tajweed.
3. **Surah Al-'Asr in Action:** When working on group assignments, how can you practice the two community duties of Surah Al-'Asr: advising to truth (*Al-Tawasi bil-Haqq*) and encouraging patience (*Al-Tawasi bil-Sabr*)?

# Level 4 Student Handout: Deepening Belief & the Quran

**Age Group:** Ages 12-14 (Level 4 Track - Adolescent & Puberty / Years 7 & 8)  
**Topics:** Textual Preservation of the Quran, I'jaz al-Qur'an, Intention (Niyyah) & Sincerity (Ikhlas), Tafsir of Surahs Al-Ikhlas, Al-'Asr & Al-Mulk, Hadith Sciences, Usul al-Madhhab & 'Amal Ahl al-Madinah, and Advanced Tajweed (Meem Sakinah & Madd)  
**Classical Text Spine:** *Al-Itqan fi 'Ulum al-Qur'an* (Imam al-Suyuti), *Tafsir Ibn Kathir*, *Al-Murshid al-Mu'in* (Ibn 'Ashir), and *Al-Muwatta'* (Imam Malik)  
**Riwayah & Tajweed:** Hafs 'an 'Asim and Warsh 'an Nafi' (Meem Sakinah, Advanced Madd, Juz' 29)

---

## 1. The Preservation of the Quran: From Oral Transmission to Written Codex

As an adolescent Muslim stepping into intellectual maturity, understanding 'Ulum al-Qur'an (The Sciences of the Quran) gives you certitude in the uncorrupted textual preservation of the Book of Allah.

| Historical Era | Leadership & Key Figures | Primary Motivation | Method of Verification & Standardization |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **1. Prophetic Lifetime** (13 BH to 11 AH) | Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and appointed scribes (*Kuttab al-Wahy*) | Recording verses as they were revealed over 23 years | Memorized by hundreds of Companions; written on parchment, leather, and palm stalks under the direct guidance of the Prophet ﷺ. |
| **2. Abu Bakr Compilation** (12 AH) | Caliph Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, Sayyidina 'Umar, and Zayd ibn Thabit (RA) | Martyrdom of dozens of memorizers (*Huffaz*) at the Battle of Yamamah | Zayd gathered scattered parchments into a single master codex (*Suhuf*), requiring two upright eyewitnesses for every written text alongside oral memory. |
| **3. 'Uthmanic Standardization** (30 AH) | Caliph 'Uthman ibn 'Affan and an expert committee led by Zayd ibn Thabit | Regional dialect disputes among soldiers in newly opened territories | Transcribed identical master codices (*Al-Masahif al-'Uthmaniyyah*) in the Qurayshi dialect; sent to major centers (Makkah, Kufah, Basrah, Damascus, Madinah). |

### The Scribe of the Quran: Zayd ibn Thabit (RA)
Zayd ibn Thabit was selected by Abu Bakr because he was young, brilliant, possessed sharp memory, was a veteran scribe of revelation during the lifetime of the Prophet ﷺ, and was universally recognized for unblemished honesty. Zayd remarked on the gravity of this task:
> *"By Allah, if they had ordered me to move one of the mountains, it would not have been heavier for me than what they ordered me to do regarding the compilation of the Quran."* (Sahih al-Bukhari 4986).

---

## 2. I'jaz al-Qur'an: The Inimitable Divine Speech

The miraculous nature of the Quran is known in Islamic theology as **I'jaz** (إِعْجَاز), meaning divine speech that renders human competition powerless.

Allah challenged the master poets and orators of pre-Islamic Arabia in three progressive stages:
1. **Challenge 1 (The Entire Book):** Produce a complete book equal to the Quran (Surah Al-Isra' 17:88: *"Say: If mankind and jinn were to gather to produce the like of this Quran, they could not produce the like of it, even if they assisted one another."*).
2. **Challenge 2 (Ten Chapters):** Produce ten fabricated surahs like it (Surah Hud 11:13).
3. **Challenge 3 (A Single Surah):** Produce even one short surah resembling its rhetorical majesty and wisdom (Surah Al-Baqarah 2:23: *"And if you are in doubt about what We have sent down upon Our servant, then produce a surah the like thereof..."*).

Despite their fierce hostility to Islam and their unmatched mastery of Arabic poetry, the tribal leaders failed to compose even three lines comparable to the shortest chapter, Surah Al-Kawthar. One of the chief Qurayshi rhetoricians, Al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah, heard the Prophet ﷺ reciting the Quran and confessed:
> *"By Allah, its words possess sweetness, upon it is grace, its upper branch bears fruit, its lower roots are abundant, and it surpasses all speech and cannot be surpassed!"* (Mustadrak al-Hakim 3872, Sahih per al-Dhahabi).

---

## 3. Deepening Faith: Intention, Sincerity, and Key Surahs

### A. Intention (Niyyah), Sincerity (Ikhlas), and Ash'ari Kasb
In Islamic theology, deeds are evaluated by inner purpose. Sayyidina 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
> *"Actions are judged only by intentions, and every person will have only what they intended."* (Sahih al-Bukhari 1, Sahih Muslim 1907).

* **Ikhlas (Sincerity):** Performing righteous deeds purely for the pleasure of Allah, free from worldly praise.
* **Riya' (Ostentation / Minor Shirk):** Performing acts of worship so people notice, admire, or praise you. Riya' ruins good deeds.
* **The Doctrine of Kasb (Acquisition):** In Ash'ari theology, Allah creates all human actions, while human beings freely choose their intention and acquire (*Kasb*) responsibility for their deeds. You are not forced (fatalism), nor are you an independent creator of your actions; you are an accountable servant with real moral choice.

### B. Tafsir of Surah Al-'Asr (Chapter 103)
Allah swears by Time (*Al-'Asr*) that all humanity is in loss, except those who embody four essential qualities:
1. **True Faith (*Iman*):** Grounded conviction in Allah and His Messenger.
2. **Righteous Action (*'Amal Salih*):** Obeying divine commands with sincere intention.
3. **Counseling Truth (*Tawasi bil-Haqq*):** Encouraging justice, knowledge, and virtue.
4. **Counseling Patience (*Tawasi bis-Sabr*):** Remaining steadfast through trials and obedience.

Imam al-Shafi'i noted:
> *"If Allah had revealed only this surah to His creation, it would have been sufficient guidance for them."* (Tafsir Ibn Kathir).

### C. Thematic Study: Surah Al-Mulk (Chapter 67)
The Prophet ﷺ said:
> *"There is a surah in the Quran containing thirty verses which intercedes for a person until they are forgiven: Tabarak alladhi bi-yadihi al-Mulk."* (Sunan Abi Dawud 1400, Jami' at-Tirmidhi 2891, Hasan).

Key themes in Surah Al-Mulk:
1. **The Divine Purpose of Life and Death (Verse 2):** *"He who created death and life to test you as to which of you is best in deed."* The ayah specifies *"best in deed"* (*Ahsanu 'Amala*), not *"most in deed."* Scholars explain that the best deed is that which is most sincere (*Akhlasuh*) and most aligned with the Sunnah (*Aswabuh*).
2. **Cosmic Flawlessness (Verses 3-4):** Allah invites humanity to observe the heavens: Can you detect any defect or rift (*Tafawut*) in the creation of the Most Merciful?
3. **Protection in the Grave:** Reciting Surah Al-Mulk each night anchors accountability and shields the believer from the trials of the grave.

---

## 4. The Sunnah, Hadith Sciences, and the Madhhabs

### A. The Anatomy of Hadith
Every hadith consists of two inseparable parts:
1. **The Isnad (Chain of Transmission):** The sequence of trustworthy narrators linking the compiler back to the Prophet ﷺ.
2. **The Matn (Text):** The spoken words, actions, or silent approvals of the Prophet ﷺ.

| Hadith Grade | Definition | Rigor of Transmission | Legal Status |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Sahih (Authentic)** | Transmitted by upright narrators with precise memory, continuous chain, free of defects (*'Ilal*) or contradictions. | Highest historical rigor | Primary proof in creed and law |
| **Hasan (Good)** | Transmitted by upright narrators whose accuracy is slightly less than Sahih, with an unbroken chain. | Solid historical reliability | Valid proof in legal rulings |
| **Da'if (Weak)** | Lacks one or more conditions of Sahih and Hasan (such as a break in the chain or narrator weakness). | Sub-standard rigor | Not used for creed; limited use in virtuous deeds with strict conditions |

The Six Canonical Sunnah Collections (*Al-Kutub al-Sittah*) are Sahih al-Bukhari, Sahih Muslim, Sunan Abi Dawud, Jami' at-Tirmidhi, Sunan an-Nasa'i, and Sunan Ibn Majah. Alongside these stands the earlier foundational work, *Al-Muwatta'* of Imam Malik.

### B. Why Follow a Madhhab?
A Madhhab is a systematic legal methodology developed by master scholars (*Mujtahidun*) to extract rulings directly from the Quran and Sunnah. The four recognized Sunni schools are:
* **The Hanafi School:** Founded by Imam Abu Hanifah (d. 150 AH) in Kufah.
* **The Maliki School:** Founded by Imam Malik ibn Anas (d. 179 AH) in Madinah.
* **The Shafi'i School:** Founded by Imam Muhammad ibn Idris al-Shafi'i (d. 204 AH).
* **The Hanbali School:** Founded by Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal (d. 241 AH) in Baghdad.

### C. Imam Malik's Relied-Upon Principle: 'Amal Ahl al-Madinah
Imam Malik gave special weight to **'Amal Ahl al-Madinah** (the living practice of the people of Madinah). Because thousands of Companions lived, prayed, and practiced Islam in Madinah under the Prophet's instruction, their continuous communal practice represents a living mass transmission (*Tawatur*) of the Sunnah from generation to generation.

---

## 5. Advanced Tajweed: Rules of Meem Sakinah and Madd

### A. The Three Rules of Meem Sakinah (مْ)
When a Meem Sakinah occurs with a Sukun, it follows one of three rules:
1. **Ikhfa' Shafawi (Oral Concealment):** Occurs when Meem Sakinah is followed by **Ba (ب)**. Pronounce the Meem by lightly closing the lips with a 2-count nasal hum (e.g., *Tarmihim bi-hijarah*).
2. **Idgham Shafawi (Oral Merging):** Occurs when Meem Sakinah is followed by another **Meem (م)**. Merge the two letters into a single doubled Meem with a 2-count Ghunnah (e.g., *Lahum ma yasha'un*).
3. **Izhar Shafawi (Oral Clarity):** Occurs when Meem Sakinah is followed by any of the remaining 26 Arabic letters. Pronounce the Meem clearly without elongation.  
   *Precaution:* Pay close attention when Meem Sakinah is followed by **Waw (و)** or **Fa (ف)**, because they share labial articulation points, which can lead reciters to conceal the Meem mistakenly.

### B. The Taxonomy of Madd (Elongation)
* **Madd Tabee'ee (Natural Madd):** Prolonged for 2 counts when a Madd letter (*Alif*, *Waw*, *Ya*) has no Hamzah or Sukun after it.
* **Madd Muttasil (Connected Obligatory):** When a Madd letter is followed by a Hamzah inside the **same single word** (prolonged 4 to 5 counts, e.g., *Ja'a*, *Al-Sama'*).
* **Madd Munfasil (Separated Permissible):** When the Madd letter ends one word and the Hamzah begins the next word (prolonged 2 or 4 to 5 counts in Hafs; 6 counts in Warsh, e.g., *Inna a'taynak*).
* **Madd Lazim (Compulsory Madd):** When an unyielding original Sukun or Shaddah follows the Madd letter (prolonged for a full 6 counts unconditionally, e.g., *Al-Dallin*, *Al-Haqqah*).

---

## 6. Section 6: Curriculum Anchors in Practice

Adolescence is a time of questioning, discovery, and identity formation. Apply these anchors to your daily routine:
1. **Intellectual Certitude:** When confronted with modern secular critiques of ancient scriptures, recognize that the Quran's simultaneous oral transmission by thousands and rigorous written verification under Zayd ibn Thabit provide unparalleled historical reliability.
2. **Purifying Motives:** Before opening your Quran, completing homework, or performing service for family, pause and formulate a sincere intention (*Niyyah*). Strive to perform deeds purely for Allah, guarding against ostentation (*Riya'*).
3. **Nightly Recitation of Surah Al-Mulk:** Make it your habit to recite the thirty verses of Surah Al-Mulk before sleeping, reflecting on the signs of cosmic perfection and preparing your soul for the meeting with your Creator.

# Level 5 Senior Seminar Guide: Deepening Belief & the Quran

**Age Group:** Ages 14-16+ (Senior High / Level 5 Capstone Track)  
**Topics:** Theology of Divine Speech (Kalam Nafsi vs Lafzi), The Seven Ahruf & Ten Qira'at, Thematic Tafsir of Surah Al-Kahf, Advanced Hadith Sciences, Usul al-Fiqh, and Defending the Manuscript Tradition  
**Classical Text Spine:** *Al-Burhan fi 'Ulum al-Qur'an* (Imam al-Zarkashi), *Al-Iqtisad fil-I'tiqad* (Imam al-Ghazali), *Al-Risalah* (Ibn Abi Zayd al-Qayrawani), and *Tafsir al-Qurtubi*  
**Riwayah & Advanced Tajweed:** Phonological comparison: Hafs 'an 'Asim vs Warsh 'an Nafi'; The History of Orthography (Rasm 'Uthmani)

---

## 1. The Dogmatic Theology of Divine Speech (*Kalam Allah*)

In senior Islamic theology, the doctrine of **Kalam Allah (The Speech of Allah)** represents one of the most historically defining discussions of Sunni scholastic theology (*Kalam*).

| Theological Dimension | Arabic Term | Definition & Nature in Ash'ari Theology | Relation to Created Realm |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Inner Eternal Speech** | *Al-Kalam al-Nafsi* (الْكَلامُ النَّفْسِيُّ) | An eternal, uncreated attribute inherent in the Divine Essence of Allah. | Transcendent of physical sound waves, vibrations, breaths, human vocal cords, temporal letters, or sequential syllables. |
| **The Revealed Expression** | *Al-Lafz al-Munazzal* (اللَّفْظُ الْمُنَزَّلُ) | The Arabic speech revealed through Angel Jibril to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, recited by human tongues and inscribed in codices. | An authentic, uncorrupted created manifestation and recitation of Allah's uncreated eternal speech; Sunni orthodoxy affirms: The Quran is the uncreated Word of Allah (*Kalam Allah Ghayr Makhluq*). |

### Refutation of the Mu'tazilite Claim (*Khalq al-Qur'an*)
The historical Mu'tazilah claimed that Allah created His speech as an external, transient object, akin to creating a tree or a stone. Sunni scholars, led by Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal and systematized by Imam Abu al-Hasan al-Ash'ari, vigorously rejected this view. If divine speech were a contingent, created object, divine moral commands and ethical truths would be temporary cultural artifacts subject to human revision or abrogation. Sunni orthodoxy maintained that divine guidance originates in an eternal, uncreated attribute of Allah.

---

## 2. The Seven Ahruf and the Canonical Qira'at

Sayyidina 'Umar ibn al-Khattab and Hisham ibn Hakim once recited Surah Al-Furqan in different ways before the Prophet ﷺ. The Prophet listened to both and affirmed:
> *"It was revealed like this. Indeed, this Quran was revealed according to Seven Ahruf (modes), so recite whatever is easy of it."* (Sahih al-Bukhari 2419, Sahih Muslim 818).

### Distinguishing Ahruf from Qira'at
* **The Seven Ahruf (Linguistic Modes):** Divine concessions granted during the Prophetic era to accommodate the distinct tribal dialects of Arabia (such as Quraysh, Hudhayl, Tamim, and Hawazin) in pronunciation, synonym variation, and inflection, easing memorization for elders, children, and those unaccustomed to the Qurayshi idiom.
* **The Canonical Qira'at (Codified Recitations):** Methodologies of recitation codified in the 2nd and 3rd centuries AH by master reciters based on the standardized **Rasm 'Uthmani** (the skeletal consonantal script distributed by Caliph 'Uthman without diacritical dots or vowels).

### The Ten Mutawatir Recitations
Each of the ten canonical Qira'at possesses an unbroken, mass-transmitted chain of transmission (*Isnad Mutawatir*) back to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ:
1. **Nafi' of Madinah** (transmitted by Warsh and Qalun) - The foundational recitation across the Maghrib (Morocco, Algeria, Mauritania) and West Africa, reflecting the ancient Madinan scholarly tradition.
2. **'Asim of Kufah** (transmitted by Hafs and Shu'bah) - Widely prevalent across the Middle East, South Asia, Turkey, and the Americas.
3. **Ibn Kathir of Makkah**, **Abu 'Amr of Basrah**, **Ibn 'Amir of Damascus**, **Hamzah of Kufah**, **Al-Kisa'i of Kufah**, **Abu Ja'far of Madinah**, **Ya'qub of Basrah**, and **Khalaf of Kufah**.

---

## 3. Thematic Tafsir: Surah Al-Kahf and the Four Civilizational Trials

The Prophet ﷺ recommended the weekly recitation of Surah Al-Kahf (Chapter 18) every Friday:
> *"Whoever recites Surah Al-Kahf on Friday, light will shine for them between the two Fridays."* (Sunan al-Darimi 3407, Mustadrak al-Hakim 3392, Sahih).

Surah Al-Kahf provides a divine diagnosis of the four archetypal trials (*Fitan*) that confront human civilizations across history:

| Trial Category | Central Narrative | Psychological Danger & Secular Trap | Spiritual & Practical Antidote |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **1. Trial of Faith (*Din*)** | The Youths of the Cave (Verses 9-26) | Societal pressure, ideological persecution, and state-enforced conformity to disbelief. | Seeking righteous companionship, detachment from tyranny, and trusting completely in Allah's protection. |
| **2. Trial of Wealth (*Mal*)** | The Owner of the Two Gardens (Verses 32-44) | Material entitlement, consumerism, and arrogance that attributes wealth to personal virtue. | Acknowledging that all bounty belongs to Allah (*Ma sha' Allah, la quwwata illa billah*) and remembering the fleeting nature of this world. |
| **3. Trial of Knowledge (*'Ilm*)** | Prophet Musa and Al-Khidr (Verses 60-82) | Intellectual pride, rational reductionism, and judging divine wisdom purely by empirical appearances. | Humility before divine decree, recognizing human intellectual limits, and patient trust in Allah's unfolding wisdom. |
| **4. Trial of Power (*Mulk*)** | Dhul-Qarnayn (Verses 83-98) | Tyranny, technological arrogance, and exploiting power for self-aggrandizement. | God-conscious governance (*Taqwa*), establishing justice, defending the vulnerable, and attributing power to divine favor. |

---

## 4. Advanced Hadith Sciences and Usul al-Fiqh

### A. Advanced Hadith Criticism
Beyond simple chain examination, master muhaddithin developed specialized sub-disciplines:
* **'Ilm al-Jarh wal-Ta'dil (Narrator Evaluation):** The rigorous biographical assessment of a narrator's religious integrity (*'Adalah*) and mnemonic precision (*Dabt*).
* **'Ilm al-'Ilal (Hidden Defects):** Detecting subtle flaws in chains or texts that appear sound on the surface, accessible only to elite scholars like Imam al-Bukhari and Imam al-Daraqutni.
* **Mutawatir vs Ahad:** A *Mutawatir* narration is reported by so many independent narrators in every generation that collusion upon a lie is rationally impossible, producing certain knowledge (*'Ilm Qat'i*). An *Ahad* narration is transmitted through limited chains, requiring strict juristic evaluation before deriving legal norms.

### B. Usul al-Fiqh and Maliki Methodology
The science of legal theory (*Usul al-Fiqh*) establishes the hermeneutical principles by which scholars extract normative rulings from revelation. While all four Sunni schools agree upon the primacy of the Quran, the authentic Sunnah, consensus (*Ijma'*), and analogical deduction (*Qiyas*), the Maliki school relies upon distinctive foundational proofs:
1. **'Amal Ahl al-Madinah (Practice of the People of Madinah):** The living, inherited communal practice of thousands of residents of Madinah holds evidentiary priority over isolated solitary hadiths (*Khabar al-Wahid*), because communal mass transmission represents an unbroken physical living Sunnah.
2. **Maslahah Mursalah (Unrestricted Public Benefit):** Deriving rulings to secure genuine societal welfare and avert harm in cases where no explicit scriptural text exists, bounded by the higher objectives of the Shari'ah (*Maqasid*).
3. **Sadd al-Dhara'i' (Blocking the Means to Harm):** Prohibiting an otherwise permissible action if it predictably and consistently leads to a forbidden outcome.

---

## 5. Defending the Textual Transmission Against Secular Revisionism

When engaging academic orientalist and secular critique, Muslim scholars point to empirical historical evidence:
1. **The Primacy of Oral Transmission:** Unlike ancient Western texts that depended on single monastic scribes, the Quran's primary preservation was oral mass transmission (*Tawatur*). Thousands of Companions and Successors memorized the entire text verbatim. Written codices served as auxiliary records (*Dabt*) to oral recitation.
2. **Manuscript Evidence:** Radiocarbon testing of early manuscripts (such as the Birmingham Quran folios and the Sana'a palimpsests) confirms parchment dates contemporary with the Prophetic lifetime and the Companions. Scribal training drafts or personal study notes erased on palimpsests reflect individual student exercises, never disputing the communal consensus (*Ijma'*) of the standardized Uthmanic codices.
3. **The Unpointed Consonantal Deducer (*Rasm*):** Caliph 'Uthman's choice to distribute manuscripts with unpointed consonantal skeletons was an intentional editorial decision that allowed the text to encompass the authentic, verified variant readings (*Qira'at*) authorized by the Prophet ﷺ.

---

## 6. Section 6: Curriculum Anchors in Practice

1. **Intellectual Maturity:** Stand confident when addressing secular epistemological challenges. Recognize that Islamic intellectual history developed peerless historical methods in textual transmission, narrator critique, and juristic reasoning centuries before the European Renaissance.
2. **Weekly Anchoring in Surah Al-Kahf:** Recite and ponder Surah Al-Kahf every Friday. Identify which of the four trials (faith, wealth, knowledge, or power) is most active in your educational and social environment, and apply its specific spiritual antidote.
3. **Appreciating Scholarly Heritage:** Respect the diversity of the canonical Qira'at and the four Sunni Madhhabs. Recognize that variations in reading and legal reasoning represent richness, mercy, and profound academic discipline within Sunni orthodoxy.

# Teacher Presentation Slides: Deepening Belief & the Quran

**Subject:** Islamic Studies (Intermediate / Family Level)  
**Creed (*‘Aqīdah*):** Ash‘arī  
**Jurisprudence (*Fiqh*):** Mālikī  
**Slide Count:** 21 Slides with detailed Teacher Notes

---

## Slide 1: Welcome & Course Overview
### Slide Content
* **Course Title:** Deepening Belief & the Quran (Islamic Studies for Family)
* **Objective:** Developing a thorough understanding of core Islamic beliefs, Quranic history, Tafseer, Hadith collection, and the Maliki legal tradition.
* **Key Themes:**
  1. Tawheed & Daily Intentions (*Niyyah*)
  2. The Quran: Revelation & Preservation
  3. Introduction to Tafseer: Surahs Al-Ikhlāṣ and Al-‘Aṣr
  4. Hadith & Sunnah: Preservation & Transmission
  5. Legal Frameworks: Why a Madhhab? (Focus on the school of Madinah)
* **Our Motto:** Sincerity in Heart, Soundness in Creed, Rigor in Practice.

### Teacher Notes
* **Aims:** Set expectations for the course. Introduce the concept of study as a form of worship (*‘ibādah*).
* **Pedagogical Tip:** Ask students: "Why do we study Islam?" to transition into Slide 2 on intention.
* **Ash‘arī/Mālikī Flag:** The course adheres strictly to classical Sunni orthodoxy: Ash‘arī theology (which balances reason and revelation) and Mālikī jurisprudence (which prioritizes both textual sources and the lived practice of the Prophet's ﷺ city).

---

## Slide 2: Unit 1: Tawheed in Daily Life: The Role of Intention (Niyyah)
### Slide Content
* **The Foundation of Action:**
  * Arabic Term: *Niyyah* (نِيّة) - Intention or purpose.
  * Hadith: *"Actions are only by intentions, and every person will have only what they intended..."* (Bukhari & Muslim).
* **Why does intention matter?**
  * It transforms ordinary habits (*‘ādah*) into acts of worship (*‘ibādah*).
  * Example: Eating to gain strength to worship Allah vs. eating purely for sensory pleasure.
* **The Seat of Intention:**
  * The heart (*al-qalb*). Stating the intention out loud is recommended in some circumstances to aid the heart, but the true locus is internal.

### Teacher Notes
* **Aims:** Help students understand that Islam is not just about external movements, but internal alignment.
* **Discussion Prompt:** "If someone sweeps the floor to get pocket money vs. sweeping the floor to make their parents happy and please Allah, what is the difference in reward?"
* **Mālikī Fiqh Flag:** In the Mālikī school, the *niyyah* is a strict pillar (*rukn*) for the validity of purification (*ṭahārah*) and prayer (*ṣalāh*). Without a specific intention at the very beginning of the act, the worship is invalid.

---

## Slide 3: Sincerity (Ikhlāṣ) vs. Showing Off (Riyā’)
### Slide Content
* **Sincerity (*Ikhlāṣ* - إِخْلَاص):**
  * Purifying one's actions so they are done *only* for the sake of Allah (*Lillāh*).
* **The Threat of Ostentation (*Riyā’* - رِيَاء):**
  * Doing good deeds so people will praise you, notice you, or think you are religious.
  * Often called the "minor shirk" (*ash-shirk al-asghar*) because it associates human approval with Allah's pleasure.
* **The Qur'anic Warning:**
  * *"So woe to those who pray, [but] who are heedless of their prayer - those who make show [of their deeds]"* (Surah Al-Mā‘ūn, 107:4-6).

### Teacher Notes
* **Aims:** Cultivate self-reflection and watchfulness (*murāqabah*) over one's heart.
* **Pedagogical Tip:** Use the analogy of a fake coin: it looks shiny on the outside but is worthless inside. Similarly, an action done with *riyā’* has no weight in the sight of Allah.
* **Ash‘arī Creed Flag:** Ash‘arīs emphasize that Allah does not accept actions that have partners associated with Him. The purity of belief (*Tawḥeed*) directly requires purity of action (*ikhlāṣ*).

---

## Slide 4: Action & Creation: The Ash‘arī Concept of Kasb (Acquisition)
### Slide Content
* **Who Creates Our Actions?**
  * **Allah is the Creator of everything**, including our physical bodies and our choices.
  * Qur'an: *"And Allah created you and that which you do."* (Surah Aṣ-Ṣāffāt, 37:96).
* **The human role: *Kasb* (كَسْب):**
  * Transliteration: *Kasb* (Acquisition).
  * Definition: While Allah creates the power and the act, the human being *chooses* and *directs* their will (*al-irādah al-juz’iyyah*) towards the action.
* **Responsibility:**
  * Because we choose to acquire the act (good or bad), we are held accountable for it.

### Teacher Notes
* **Aims:** Introduce the middle-path theology of the Ash‘arī school regarding free will and predestination.
* **Ash‘arī Creed Flag (Critical Concept):** 
  * The Ash‘arīs navigate between two extremes: the *Qadariyyah* (who claimed humans create their own actions independently of Allah) and the *Jabariyyah* (who claimed humans have no choice at all, like feathers in the wind). 
  * Ash‘arism teaches that Allah is the sole *Khāliq* (Creator) of the action, but the human is the *Mūtasib* (Acquirer). We intend and choose; Allah creates the action in accordance with our choice. This ensures complete divine sovereignty and complete human moral responsibility.

---

## Slide 5: Intention in Action: A Practical Matrix
### Slide Content
| Category of Act | Action Example | Purely Habitual Intention | Transformed Intention (Worship) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Eating** | Consuming bread | "I am hungry and it tastes good." | "I eat to strengthen my body to worship Allah." |
| **Sleeping** | Going to bed early | "I am tired." | "I sleep to rest my body so I can wake up for Fajr prayer." |
| **Studying** | Reading science | "I want a high grade." | "I seek knowledge to understand Allah's creation and benefit the Ummah." |
| **Exercise** | Jogging in the park | "I want to look fit." | "I maintain my health because the strong believer is beloved to Allah." |

### Teacher Notes
* **Aims:** Provide concrete, everyday examples of *niyyah* and *kasb* in action.
* **Pedagogical Tip:** Ask students to fill in another row. For instance, how can cleaning your bedroom be transformed into an act of worship? (Intending hygiene, which is part of faith, and pleasing parents).
* **Connection:** Reiterate that through *kasb*, they choose to redirect their day-to-day habits to earn immense spiritual rewards.

---

## Slide 6: Unit 2: The Quran: Divine Speech and Revelation
### Slide Content
* **What is the Quran?**
  * The speech of Allah (*Kalāmullāh*), revealed to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ through the Angel Jibreel (Gabriel).
  * The miracle that remains unchanged and protected by Allah.
* **How it was revealed:**
  * Over a period of **23 years**.
  * Revealed in portions: some in Makkah (focusing on Creed and Tawheed) and some in Madinah (focusing on law, community, and social structures).
* **The Qur'anic Witness:**
  * *"Indeed, it is We who sent down the Quran and indeed, We will be its guardian."* (Surah Al-Ḥijr, 15:9).

### Teacher Notes
* **Aims:** Set the historical and theological foundation of the Quran.
* **Pedagogical Tip:** Contrast the Quran with other scriptures which were altered over time. Highlight the miracle of Quranic memorization (*ḥifẓ*) as a primary method of preservation.
* **Discussion:** Why do you think the Quran was revealed gradually over 23 years instead of all at once? (To strengthen the Prophet's ﷺ heart and allow the Sahabah to implement the laws step-by-step).

---

## Slide 7: Ash‘arī Theology: Al-Kalām al-Nafsī vs. Al-Kalām al-Lafẓī
### Slide Content
* **Divine Attribute of Speech (*Kalām*):**
  * In Ash‘arī theology, Speech is an eternal, uncreated attribute of Allah.
* **The Distinction:**
  1. ***Al-Kalām al-Nafsī* (الكَلَام النَّفْسِي):**
     * The internal, eternal Speech of Allah. It has no beginning, no end, and does not consist of letters, sounds, or languages (like Arabic or Hebrew).
  2. ***Al-Kalām al-Lafẓī* (الكَلَام اللَّفْظِي):**
     * The created expression of that eternal Speech. This refers to the physical words we recite, the ink we write, and the sound waves we hear. It is in Arabic, which is created by Allah to allow humans to comprehend His eternal message.
* **Our Belief:** The Quran we hold in our hands points to and represents the uncreated Speech of Allah.

### Teacher Notes
* **Aims:** Teach correct creedal formulation regarding the nature of the Quran, preventing errors like total physical anthropomorphism or, conversely, denying the Quran is the Speech of Allah.
* **Ash‘arī Creed Flag (Critical Concept):**
  * The historical debate on whether the Quran is created or uncreated caused much confusion. The Ash‘arī scholars resolved this systematically. 
  * The *Attribute* of Speech itself (*al-Kalām al-Nafsī*) is eternal and uncreated, just like Allah's Knowledge and Power. 
  * The *physical recitation*, the paper, and the ink (*al-Kalām al-Lafẓī*) are created by Allah. However, we do not call the Quran "created" without qualification, because the message and the meaning it carries is the eternal Speech of Allah.

---

## Slide 8: Period of Revelation: Oral Transmission & Scribes
### Slide Content
* **The Primary Method: Oral Preservation**
  * The Prophet ﷺ memorized the Quran instantly when Jibreel recited it.
  * He ﷺ would immediately recite it to the Sahabah (Companions), who would memorize it.
  * The Quran was preserved primarily in the chests of men (*ṣudūr al-rijāl*).
* **The Secondary Method: Written Fragments**
  * The Prophet ﷺ appointed specific scribes of revelation (*Kuttāb al-Waḥy*), such as Zayd ibn Thābit.
  * They wrote the verses on available materials: parchment (*raq*), palm leaves (*‘usub*), shoulder bones of camels (*aktāf*), and flat stones (*likhāf*).
  * This occurred in the direct presence of the Prophet ﷺ to ensure absolute accuracy.

### Teacher Notes
* **Aims:** Detail the dual-track preservation system (memorization + writing) during the life of the Prophet ﷺ.
* **Discussion:** Why was oral preservation more reliable than written fragments in ancient Arabia? (Paper was scarce, but the Arabs had highly developed, legendary memories for poetry and genealogies).
* **Historical context:** Mention that the text was written in the early Arabic script, without dots (*naqṭ*) or vowel marks (*tashkeel*), which was read according to the oral tradition.

---

## Slide 9: Compilation of the Mushaf: Abu Bakr & Uthmanic Collections
### Slide Content
* **First Phase: Abu Bakr's Caliphate (11-13 AH)**
  * Trigger: The Battle of Yamamah, where many memorizers (*huffāẓ*) of the Quran were martyred.
  * Action: Caliph Abu Bakr (advised by Umar) commissioned Zayd ibn Thābit to collect all written fragments and compile them into one master manuscript (*Ṣuḥuf*).
  * Criterion: Every written piece had to be verified by two witnesses who heard it directly from the Prophet ﷺ.
* **Second Phase: Uthman's Caliphate (25-35 AH)**
  * Trigger: Expansion of the empire led to regional differences in pronunciation and dialects.
  * Action: Caliph Uthman ordered the master manuscript to be copied into standard codices (*Maṣāḥif*, sing. *Muṣḥaf*) written in the Qurayshi dialect.
  * Standardization: The *Rasm al-‘Uthmānī* (Uthmanic orthography) became the sole authorized script. All other individual personal notebooks were destroyed to preserve unity.

### Teacher Notes
* **Aims:** Provide a clear timeline of the preservation of the written text.
* **Pedagogical Tip:** Emphasize that the Uthmanic compilation did not change the Quran; it standardized the writing to prevent arguments about dialectal differences (*Ahruf*).
* **Mālikī Flag:** The Mālikī school (and the consensus of Sunni scholars) maintains that the Uthmanic script (*Rasm ‘Uthmānī*) is sacred and must be preserved in all written copies of the Quran; we cannot update the spelling rules of the Quran to match modern Arabic grammar rules.

---

## Slide 10: Unit 3: Introduction to Tafseer (Quranic Exegesis)
### Slide Content
* **What is Tafseer?**
  * Arabic Term: *Tafseer* (تَفْسِير) - Explanation, interpretation, or uncovering.
  * Science: The scholarly study of the meanings, context, and rulings of Quranic verses.
* **Sources of Tafseer:**
  1. The Quran itself (explaining one verse by another).
  2. The Sunnah (the Prophet ﷺ explaining verses to his companions).
  3. The statements of the Sahabah (Companions) and Tābi‘ūn (Successors).
  4. Sound Arabic grammar and linguistic analysis.
* **Warning:** It is forbidden to interpret the Quran based on personal, uneducated whim (*tafseer bi'r-ra’y al-maḍmūm*).

### Teacher Notes
* **Aims:** Establish the intellectual authority required to explain the Word of Allah.
* **Pedagogical Tip:** Use the analogy of a specialized medical text. Just as you wouldn't let a random person interpret a brain surgery manual, we do not let untrained people interpret the text of Allah's revelation without checking the scholars.
* **Core Rule:** Tafseer requires mastery of over 15 classical disciplines, including lexicography, grammar, theology (*‘aqīdah*), jurisprudence (*fiqh*), and historical contexts of revelation (*asbāb al-nuzūl*).

---

## Slide 11: Surah Al-Ikhlāṣ: Text and Translation
### Slide Content
```text
بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ
1. قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ
2. اللَّهُ الصَّمَدُ
3. لَمْ يَلِدْ وَلَمْ يُولَدْ
4. وَلَمْ يَكُن لَّهُ كُفُوًا أَحَدٌ
```
* **Translation:**
  1. Say, "He is Allah, [who is] One.
  2. Allah, the Self-Sufficient Besought of all.
  3. He neither begets nor is born,
  4. Nor is there to Him any equivalent."
* **Context of Revelation (*Asbāb al-Nuzūl*):**
  * The polytheists of Makkah came to the Prophet ﷺ and asked: "Describe the lineage of your Lord." Allah revealed this Surah in response.

### Teacher Notes
* **Aims:** Introduce the text, pronunciation, and translation of Surah Al-Ikhlāṣ.
* **Pedagogical Tip:** Recite the Surah with the students, paying close attention to Tajweed rules (e.g., the Qalqalah at the end of *aḥad*, *ṣamad*, *yulad*).
* **Theological Import:** Highlight that this short Surah represents one-third of the Quran (*thuluth al-Quran*) because the Quran deals with three primary themes: Creed (*‘Aqīdah*), Law (*Fiqh*), and Stories/Exhortations. This Surah fully covers the first theme.

---

## Slide 12: Surah Al-Ikhlāṣ: Ash‘arī Creed & Tanzīh (Transcendence)
### Slide Content
* **Core Theology: *Tanzīh* (تَنْزِيه):**
  * Definition: Declaring Allah free from any resemblance to His creation (transcendence).
  * Ash‘arī Principle: Allah is not a body, does not occupy space, is not bound by time, and has no physical parts.
* **Analyzing Verse 1: *Aḥad* (أَحَد):**
  * Allah is absolute Unity. He is not composed of parts, and He has no partners or equals.
* **Analyzing Verses 3 & 4: Rejecting Likeness:**
  * *"He neither begets nor is born"* directly refutes polytheism and any idea that Allah has a physical lineage or physical offspring.
  * *"Nor is there to Him any equivalent"* aligns with the core verse: *"There is nothing like unto Him"* (Surah Ash-Shūrā, 42:11).

### Teacher Notes
* **Aims:** Connect Surah Al-Ikhlāṣ to the foundational concepts of Ash‘arī creed.
* **Ash‘arī Creed Flag (Critical Concept):**
  * The Ash‘arī school strongly emphasizes *tanzīh* (absolving Allah of human-like qualities). 
  * Any verse or Hadith that seems to imply physical body parts (like hand, face, or sitting) must not be understood literally (*ḥaqīqī*). They are understood either:
    * Through *Tafwīḍ*: Accepting the words but consigning their true meaning and modality (*kayf*) to Allah, while firmly denying physical resemblance.
    * Through *Ta’wīl*: Explaining the terms linguistically (e.g., "Hand" meaning power or favor, "Face" meaning pleasure or existence) according to the usage of classical Arabic.

---

## Slide 13: Understanding Allah's Name: Aṣ-Ṣamad (الصَّمَد)
### Slide Content
* **What does *Aṣ-Ṣamad* mean?**
  * One of Allah's Beautiful Names, appearing only once in the Quran.
* **Classical Explanations:**
  * **The Master of All:** The Supreme Leader who possesses perfect mastery, to whom all of creation turns for their needs.
  * **The Self-Sufficient:** He who does not need anyone or anything, but everyone and everything needs Him.
  * **The One without Parts:** Linguistically, it refers to that which is solid, having no cavities, showing that Allah does not eat, drink, or have internal organs.
* **Creed Connection:**
  * Since Allah is *Aṣ-Ṣamad*, He is free from decay, change, or need.

### Teacher Notes
* **Aims:** Unpack this unique, profound Name of Allah.
* **Discussion Prompt:** "If a person is hungry, they need food. If they are tired, they need sleep. What does it mean for Allah to be completely free of all needs (*Ghanī*) while we are completely dependent (*Faqīr*)?"
* **Sources:** Refer to classical Tafseer works (e.g., Tafseer al-Qurṭubī - a major Mālikī/Ash‘arī source) where *Aṣ-Ṣamad* is explained as the Lord whose sovereignty is absolute and complete.

---

## Slide 14: Surah Al-‘Aṣr: Text and Translation
### Slide Content
```text
بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ
1. وَالْعَصْرِ
2. إِنَّ الْإِنسَانَ لَفِي خُسْرٍ
3. إِلَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ وَتَوَاصَوْا بِالْحَقِّ وَتَوَاصَوْا بِالصَّبْرِ
```
* **Translation:**
  1. By time,
  2. Indeed, mankind is in loss,
  3. Except for those who have believed and done righteous deeds and advised each other to truth and advised each other to patience.
* **Imam al-Shāfi‘ī’s Quote:**
  * *"If Allah had revealed only this Surah as a proof to His creation, it would have been enough for them."*

### Teacher Notes
* **Aims:** Introduce the text, pronunciation, and translation of Surah Al-‘Aṣr.
* **Key Vocabulary:**
  * *Al-‘Aṣr* (العَصْر): Time, or specifically the late afternoon period.
  * *Khusr* (خُسْر): Absolute loss or ruin.
  * *Tawāṣaw* (تَوَاصَوْا): Mutually advising/exhorting one another.

---

## Slide 15: Surah Al-‘Aṣr: The Formula for Escaping Loss
### Slide Content
* **The Divine Oath:**
  * Allah swears by *Time* (*Al-‘Aṣr*) to show its immense value. Time is the capital asset of human life; once spent, it can never be recovered.
* **The Four Conditions of Success:**
  1. **Faith (*Īmān*):** Correct belief in Allah and His Messenger.
  2. **Righteous Actions (*‘Amal Ṣāliḥ*):** Doing good deeds sincerely (*ikhlas*) according to the law (*Shari‘ah*).
  3. **Advising to Truth (*Tawāṣī bi’l-Ḥaqq*):** Supporting truth, justice, and correct knowledge in the family and community.
  4. **Advising to Patience (*Tawāṣī bi’ṣ-Ṣabr*):** Encouraging one another to remain firm during trials, constant in worship, and away from sins.

### Teacher Notes
* **Aims:** Practical moral and ethical application of the Surah.
* **Pedagogical Tip:** Create a link back to Unit 1 (Intention). Doing righteous actions (*‘Amal Ṣāliḥ*) requires *niyyah* to be valid. 
* **Ash‘arī Creed Note:** *Īmān* (faith) is the root, and actions (*‘amal*) are its branches. While actions are necessary for the completeness and health of faith, a person who fails in actions but has correct faith is still within the fold of Islam, though sinful. This is a key counterpoint to extremist views (like the Kharijites) who claimed that committing major sins nullifies faith completely.

---

## Slide 16: Unit 4: Hadith and Sunnah: Definitions and Collection
### Slide Content
* **Definitions:**
  * **Sunnah (سُنَّة):** The lived practice, character, rulings, and path of the Prophet ﷺ.
  * **Hadith (حَدِيث):** The written or oral report detailing what the Prophet ﷺ said, did, approved of, or looked like.
* **Authority of the Sunnah:**
  * The Quran commands us to follow the Sunnah.
  * *"He who obeys the Messenger has obeyed Allah..."* (Surah An-Nisā’, 4:80).
  * We cannot understand how to pray, pay Zakah, or perform Hajj without the Sunnah.

### Teacher Notes
* **Aims:** Clarify the vocabulary and explain the absolute authority of the prophetic model.
* **Pedagogical Tip:** Ask students: "Does the Quran specify exactly how many units (*rak‘ahs*) to pray for Dhuhr?" (No, the Quran commands prayer, but the Prophet ﷺ taught the details: "Pray as you have seen me pray").
* **Key Distinction:** A Hadith is a *report* of the Sunnah, but the Sunnah itself is the broader *normative practice*.

---

## Slide 17: How Hadith Were Collected: Isnad and Matn
### Slide Content
* **The Anatomy of a Hadith:**
  1. ***Isnād* (إِسْنَاد):** The chain of narrators leading back to the Prophet ﷺ (e.g., A heard from B, who heard from C, who heard from the Prophet ﷺ).
  2. ***Matn* (مَتْن):** The actual text or speech of the report.
* **The Evaluation Criteria:**
  * Hadith scholars developed the science of biography (*‘Ilm al-Rijāl*) to check:
    * Is the narrator trustworthy (*‘Adl*)?
    * Do they have a strong memory (*Ḍābiṭ*)?
    * Did the narrators actually meet each other (connected chain - *Muttaṣil*)?
    * Are there hidden defects (*‘Ilal*) or contradictions?
* **Classifications:**
  * *Ṣaḥīḥ* (Authentic), *Ḥasan* (Good), *Ḍa‘īf* (Weak), and *Mawḍū‘* (Fabricated).

### Teacher Notes
* **Aims:** Demystify how Hadith collections were compiled with scientific rigor.
* **Pedagogical Tip:** Use the "telephone game" analogy, but show how Hadith scholars prevented corruption by demanding a complete background check on every single person in the chain.
* **Mālikī Fiqh Flag:** While the authenticity of a chain (*isnād*) is highly important, the Mālikī school has additional criteria for acting upon a Hadith. If a single narration (*khabar al-wāḥid*) contradicts the established, continuous practice of Madinah (*‘Amal Ahl al-Madīnah*), the practice of Madinah is preferred (discussed in Slide 20).

---

## Slide 18: Unit 5: Legal Frameworks: Why Muslims Follow a Madhhab
### Slide Content
* **What is a *Madhhab* (مَذْهَب)?**
  * Plural: *Madhāhib* (مَذَاهِب).
  * Definition: A school of Islamic law named after a master jurist (*Mujtahid*).
* **The Four Canonical Sunni Madhhabs:**
  1. **Hanafi** (founded by Imam Abu Hanifah, d. 150 AH)
  2. **Maliki** (founded by Imam Malik, d. 179 AH)
  3. **Shafi'i** (founded by Imam al-Shafi'i, d. 204 AH)
  4. **Hanbali** (founded by Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal, d. 241 AH)
* **Why follow one?**
  * The Quran commands: *"So ask the people of the message if you do not know."* (Surah An-Naḥl, 16:43).
  * A Madhhab is a structured, tested methodology of extracting rulings from the Quran and Sunnah, protecting us from misinterpreting texts on our own.

### Teacher Notes
* **Aims:** Explain the concept of legal schools and normalize diversity within Sunni Islam.
* **Pedagogical Tip:** Compare a Madhhab to a medical specialty or a legal jurisdiction. You don't perform surgery by self-diagnosing via textbooks; you follow established medical protocols. Similarly, we follow established legal protocols in Fiqh.
* **Diversity Concept:** The differences between Madhhabs are in secondary legal details (*furū‘*), not core theological beliefs (*uṣūl*). All four schools are correct paths to the truth.

---

## Slide 19: Imam Malik ibn Anas: The Scholar of Madinah
### Slide Content
* **Who was Imam Malik?**
  * Born: 93 AH in Madinah. Died: 179 AH in Madinah.
  * Title: *Imām Dār al-Hijrah* (The Leader of the Abode of Migration).
  * Respect for the Prophet ﷺ: He would never ride a horse or camel in Madinah out of respect for the ground in which the Prophet ﷺ is buried, and he would always perform Wudu and wear his best clothes before teaching Hadith.
* **His Major Work:**
  * ***Al-Muwaṭṭa’* (المُوَطَّأ):** Meaning "The Approved/Smoothed Path." It is the earliest surviving written collection of Hadith and legal rulings, compiled over 40 years.

### Teacher Notes
* **Aims:** Profile the founding father of the Mālikī school.
* **Pedagogical Tip:** Highlight Imam Malik’s absolute love and reverence for the Prophet ﷺ and the city of Madinah. 
* **Historical quote:** Imam al-Shafi'i said of him: "When the scholars are mentioned, Malik is the shining star."

---

## Slide 20: Imam Malik's Methodology: ‘Amal Ahl al-Madīnah
### Slide Content
* **The Concept:** *‘Amal Ahl al-Madīnah* (عَمَل أَهْل المَدِينَة)
  * Translates to: **The practice of the people of Madinah**.
* **Why Imam Malik relied on this:**
  * Madinah was where the Prophet ﷺ lived for the last 10 years of his life, established the Shari'ah, and died.
  * Thousands of Sahabah lived there, and they passed their daily practices down to their children (the Tābi‘ūn).
  * Imam Malik argued: The continuous, daily practice of thousands of people in Madinah is a **mass-transmitted (mutawātir) physical Sunnah**.
* **Formula:**
  * Malik famously stated: *"A mass-transmission from a thousand people to a thousand people is stronger than a single person narrating from a single person (Hadith Āḥād)."*

### Teacher Notes
* **Aims:** Introduce the signature epistemological methodology of the Mālikī school.
* **Mālikī Fiqh Flag (Critical Concept):**
  * This slide explains why the Mālikī school sometimes rules differently from what is written in a specific individual Hadith. 
  * If a single Hadith narrates that the Prophet ﷺ did X, but Imam Malik observed that *none* of the scholars or general population of Madinah practiced X, he concluded that the Hadith was either abrogated (*mansūkh*), misunderstood, or rare, and that the continuous public practice (*‘Amal*) represented the final, actual Sunnah of the Prophet ﷺ.
  * Example: Praying with arms down at the sides (*sadl*). Imam Malik observed the people of Madinah praying like this, indicating it was the continuous practice passed down from the Sahabah, despite single hadiths describing clasping the hands (*qabḍ*).

---

## Slide 21: Summary & Sources
### Slide Content
* **Key Takeaways:**
  * Set a clean *niyyah* to turn ordinary life into worship.
  * Respect the dual oral-written preservation of the Quran.
  * Differentiate the uncreated speech of Allah from physical letters.
  * Understand the rigorous science of Hadith.
  * Respect the Madhhab system and the wisdom of *‘Amal Ahl al-Madīnah*.
* **Primary Reference Sources:**
  1. *Al-Muwaṭṭa’* of Imam Malik.
  2. *Tafseer al-Qurṭubī* (Mālikī Tafseer).
  3. *Jawharat al-Tawḥeed* (Standard Ash‘arī theological text).
  4. *Al-Qawānīn al-Fiqhiyyah* by Ibn Juzayy al-Gharnāṭī (Mālikī law manual).

### Teacher Notes
* **Aims:** Close the lesson and provide guidance for further study.
* **Encouragement:** Challenge the students to identify three actions they will perform tomorrow and write down how they will adjust their intentions (*niyyah*) to gain reward from Allah.

parsedSlides.title: Slide 2: Unit 1: Tawheed in Daily Life: The Role of Intention (Niyyah)
parsedSlides.content:
## Slide 2: Unit 1: Tawheed in Daily Life: The Role of Intention (Niyyah)
### Slide Content
* **The Foundation of Action:**
  * Arabic Term: *Niyyah* (نِيّة) - Intention or purpose.
  * Hadith: *"Actions are only by intentions, and every person will have only what they intended..."* (Bukhari & Muslim).
* **Why does intention matter?**
  * It transforms ordinary habits (*‘ādah*) into acts of worship (*‘ibādah*).
  * Example: Eating to gain strength to worship Allah vs. eating purely for sensory pleasure.
* **The Seat of Intention:**
  * The heart (*al-qalb*). Stating the intention out loud is recommended in some circumstances to aid the heart, but the true locus is internal.

### Teacher Notes
* **Aims:** Help students understand that Islam is not just about external movements, but internal alignment.
* **Discussion Prompt:** "If someone sweeps the floor to get pocket money vs. sweeping the floor to make their parents happy and please Allah, what is the difference in reward?"
* **Mālikī Fiqh Flag:** In the Mālikī school, the *niyyah* is a strict pillar (*rukn*) for the validity of purification (*ṭahārah*) and prayer (*ṣalāh*). Without a specific intention at the very beginning of the act, the worship is invalid.

---

parsedSlides.title: Slide 3: Sincerity (Ikhlāṣ) vs. Showing Off (Riyā’)
parsedSlides.content:
## Slide 3: Sincerity (Ikhlāṣ) vs. Showing Off (Riyā’)
### Slide Content
* **Sincerity (*Ikhlāṣ* - إِخْلَاص):**
  * Purifying one's actions so they are done *only* for the sake of Allah (*Lillāh*).
* **The Threat of Ostentation (*Riyā’* - رِيَاء):**
  * Doing good deeds so people will praise you, notice you, or think you are religious.
  * Often called the "minor shirk" (*ash-shirk al-asghar*) because it associates human approval with Allah's pleasure.
* **The Qur'anic Warning:**
  * *"So woe to those who pray, [but] who are heedless of their prayer - those who make show [of their deeds]"* (Surah Al-Mā‘ūn, 107:4-6).

### Teacher Notes
* **Aims:** Cultivate self-reflection and watchfulness (*murāqabah*) over one's heart.
* **Pedagogical Tip:** Use the analogy of a fake coin: it looks shiny on the outside but is worthless inside. Similarly, an action done with *riyā’* has no weight in the sight of Allah.
* **Ash‘arī Creed Flag:** Ash‘arīs emphasize that Allah does not accept actions that have partners associated with Him. The purity of belief (*Tawḥeed*) directly requires purity of action (*ikhlāṣ*).

---

parsedSlides.title: Slide 4: Action & Creation: The Ash‘arī Concept of Kasb (Acquisition)
parsedSlides.content:
## Slide 4: Action & Creation: The Ash‘arī Concept of Kasb (Acquisition)
### Slide Content
* **Who Creates Our Actions?**
  * **Allah is the Creator of everything**, including our physical bodies and our choices.
  * Qur'an: *"And Allah created you and that which you do."* (Surah Aṣ-Ṣāffāt, 37:96).
* **The human role: *Kasb* (كَسْب):**
  * Transliteration: *Kasb* (Acquisition).
  * Definition: While Allah creates the power and the act, the human being *chooses* and *directs* their will (*al-irādah al-juz’iyyah*) towards the action.
* **Responsibility:**
  * Because we choose to acquire the act (good or bad), we are held accountable for it.

### Teacher Notes
* **Aims:** Introduce the middle-path theology of the Ash‘arī school regarding free will and predestination.
* **Ash‘arī Creed Flag (Critical Concept):** 
  * The Ash‘arīs navigate between two extremes: the *Qadariyyah* (who claimed humans create their own actions independently of Allah) and the *Jabariyyah* (who claimed humans have no choice at all, like feathers in the wind). 
  * Ash‘arism teaches that Allah is the sole *Khāliq* (Creator) of the action, but the human is the *Mūtasib* (Acquirer). We intend and choose; Allah creates the action in accordance with our choice. This ensures complete divine sovereignty and complete human moral responsibility.

---
